drafted_from: tools/internet-archive/records.json and tool-rows.json (tool:read-internet-archive-item: its url, input pattern and verify check); no test file exists, and no live call was made
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read the Internet Archive item with identifier example-tennis-film-1952 and tell me its creator, collection, license and rights before I decide to use it." It reads the item metadata without downloading any media.
no_lists_because: It looks up one public Archive item by identifier and keeps no list of yours.
instructions: 1. Get an item identifier from tool:search-internet-archive or from an archive.org/details/<identifier> address; send only the identifier, never a URL or path.
2. Say "Read the Internet Archive item <identifier>". The AI calls tools:run for tool:read-internet-archive-item with {"identifier": "<identifier>"}.
3. Read metadata (identifier, creator, date, collection, licenseurl, rights when present) and files (the file listing). No media bytes are downloaded.
4. Record the identifier and https://archive.org/details/<identifier> as provenance; missing or unclear rights stay unknown and need your own check.

worked_examples.title: Read one item by identifier
worked_examples.ask: Read the Internet Archive item example-tennis-film-1952.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/internet-archive/records.json, not run live: a GET to https://archive.org/metadata/example-tennis-film-1952. The identifier is made up for this example; use one a search returned. It matches the input pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99}$.
worked_examples.hands_back: The Archive's JSON unchanged ($ is the result): metadata.identifier is "example-tennis-film-1952" (the tool's verify check compares it to the input), metadata also holds the item's creator, date, collection, licenseurl and rights where it has them, and files is an array of file objects. For an identifier the Archive does not hold it answers an empty object.
